newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU prospects no better-UK central bank chief.
newsitem.headline: EMU prospects no better-UK central bank chief.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Tuesday he had observed no recent improvements in prospects for European Union nations meeting the convergence criteria to join a planned currency union by a 1997 deadline.
Asked if he thought prospects for EMU convergence were better recently, he replied: "That would be too strong to say."
George, who was speaking to reporters after a regular monthly meeting at the European Monetary Institute (EMI) declined to comment on prospects of an imminent British interest rate cut.
George had been quoted by the British media on Monday as saying that at Tuesday's meeting he would fight restrictions on banks operating in nations outside a future single EU currency.
Afterwards, George would not be drawn on the specifics of the meeting, particularly regarding non-EMU central banks.

The British government has not yet made a firm commitment towards the single European currency and has been seen increasingly under the influence of so-called Euro-sceptics, who say currency union would destroy British sovereignty in deciding its monetary policy.

Some European financial leaders, including EMI president Alexandre Lamfalussy, have recently expressed optimism that nations were making progress in reaching the entry criteria for the currency union, scheduled to begin at the end of the decade.

Hopes that European countries would make greater progress toward achieving Maastricht debt criteria were boosted in late August when the Bundesbank cut its key securities repurchase rate to three percent from 3.30 percent.

France, seen as a pivotal force in pushing for monetary union, quickly followed the Bundesbank's lead, cutting its intervention rate to 3.35 percent from 3.55 percent, thereby rescuing what had been a sagging French franc.
The rate cuts were seen as attempts to fan economic growth in both countries and signalled their intentions to make a determined effort to speed up moves towards monetary union.
